subject: Re: AWS marketplace private offer — multi-year prepay & annualization
messages:
From: Alec Thompson <alec.thompson@acmeretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Retail Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>, Erin Kelly <erin.kelly@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer — multiyear prepay options

Jordan —

Thanks for taking the intro last week. Acme is seriously evaluating Redwood for our recommendation engine and we want to explore an AWS Marketplace private offer with multi-year prepay terms. A few requirements from our side:

- We need predictable unit pricing for 3 years; we'd prefer a staircase/annualized approach that matches our growth (we'll be ramping).
- There will be an initial budget approval for year 1, with possible expansion in year 2/3. Can you provide discount tiers for 1/2/3-year prepay?
- We also need an annual true-up process (we want credits applied if we overcommit), and a clear cancellation/renewal trigger at each year.
- AWS Marketplace mechanics matter to our procurement team (SKU phasing, private offer flow, and any minimums).

Attached is our procurement RDQ for context (Acme_Procurement_RDQ.pdf). Can you share an initial pricing shape and a proposed ramp schedule?

Appreciate it — happy to take a short call next week.

—Alec
Alec Thompson
Head of Data Platforms | Acme Retail
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Thompson <alec.thompson@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — multiyear prepay options

Alec —

Thanks for the RDQ and the clear ask. We can definitely do private offers on AWS with multi-year prepay and an annual true-up. Quick questions so I size options properly:

- Target committed ARR you have budgeted for year 1 (ballpark is fine).
- Any hard constraints on invoice cadence (annual vs quarterly billing)?
- Are you looking for credits to be applied at the AWS private-offer level or as a Redwood-issued credit?

I'm attaching a simple scenarios spreadsheet (Initial_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx) with three starter options (1yr, 2yr, 3yr) and a sample staircase ramp. Would you be available for a 30-min call Tue/Wed to walk through?

If that works I'll loop in our pricing/marketplace folks internally to confirm the SKU/phasing and legal checklist.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: AWS private offer — multiyear prepay options

Folks —

Acme (Alec) wants a multi-year prepay private offer on AWS with an annual true-up and a staircase/ramp schedule. Key asks: 1/2/3 year discount tiers, SKU phasing for marketplace, and how credits/true-ups are surfaced.

I've sketched three starter options in the attached workbook (Initial_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx) — please review and advise on:

- Recommended discount bands we can give on private offer vs what needs legal/finance sign-off
- Suggested ramp schedule (front-load credits vs smoothing) to protect our unit economics
- Any AWS marketplace constraints we should call out (min SKU values, private offer lead time)

Attachment: pricing_model_1yr_3yr.xlsx

Happy to sync on short call — I'd like to get back to Acme with a consolidated proposal by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: AWS private offer — multiyear prepay options

Jordan / Karthik —

High-level guidance based on similar AWS private-offer deals:

- Discount bands (net to customer on committed units):
  - 1-year annual prepay: ~20% off list
  - 2-year prepay (paid annually or upfront): ~28% off list
  - 3-year upfront prepay: ~34–36% off list (we should cap at 36% to protect ops)

- Ramp/annualization: recommend a smoothing clause where we annualize usage for discount eligibility and allow a quarterly true-up. For Acme's case we can offer a staircase commit: year1 = 45% of target, year2 = 80%, year3 = 100% — with pro-rata credits applied at annual true-up if they underutilize.

- Marketplace notes: AWS private offers require SKU creation and a lead time for listing. If they want staggered SKU activation (start with a 12-month SKU and add multi-year SKUs later) we can handle it, but procurement prefers a single private-offer agreement with schedule attachments.

- Commercial guardrails: No upfront credits that exceed 6 months of gross margin without finance sign-off. Any multi-year prepay that exceeds $1.5M ARR needs director-level approval.

I'll draft the pricing shape and an attachment we can send to Acme. Jordan — please confirm the year-1 committed $ value (ballpark) and invoice cadence.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: AWS private offer — multiyear prepay options

Marissa / Jordan —

Agree with Marissa's bands but we need a tighter ramp to preserve unit economics. Proposed counterpoints:

- Year 1 commitment should be at least 50% of the three-year target (not 45%) or we increase the minimum price per unit. If Acme cannot meet that, discount backs off by 3–5 pp.
- Include a rolling annualization clause: every year we rebase on trailing 12 months to avoid long-term undercommit exposure.
- Add an early-termination true-up that runs to the lesser of cost-to-serve or committed spend, with a 90-day notice window.

I've run rough unit-econ (attached calc_unit_econ.csv) which shows the floor for discounts at various ramp profiles — if they front-load too little in Y1 we lose margin by year 2 in GPU-hours heavy workloads.

Jordan — once you get the ballpark committed $ for year 1, I'll produce a final counter template we can send to Acme.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood private offer proposal — Acme Retail (summary + next steps)

Alec / team —

Thanks again for the conversation. Per internal reviews we've put together a consolidated private-offer approach that balances Acme's need for predictable pricing with our unit economics. Summary below and attached is the formal proposal PDF (Redwood_Acme_Po_Proposal_2027.pdf).

Summary (headline):
- Offer: AWS Marketplace Private Offer (Redwood SKU) with multi-year prepay options
- Discount bands: 1yr = 20% off list; 2yr = 28% off list; 3yr upfront = 34% off list (36% cap only with finance sign-off)
- Ramp: Recommended commit profile: Y1=50% of 3yr target, Y2=80%, Y3=100% with quarterly true-ups and pro-rata credits for underutilization applied at annualization
- Billing: Preferred annual invoicing (can accommodate quarterly invoicing if required by procurement)
- Legal/marketplace: We will create a single private-offer agreement with schedule attachments for SKU phasing; expected AWS lead time ~2–3 weeks after signatures
- Termination/true-up: Rolling annualization + 90-day early termination true-up (details in attached)

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached proposal PDF and mark any redlines.
2) If green, I will issue a DocuSign for Acme signature and start the AWS private-offer SKU creation. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/rooms/Invite?roomId=abc-123-redwood-acme
3) We'll schedule a 30-min call to walk through implementation and marketplace timelines (I have availability Thu/Fri next week).

Attachments: Redwood_Acme_Po_Proposal_2027.pdf
